title: Design System: Thesis Defense (Year 3): The Typeset Thesis
scope: Year 3 thesis-defense Phaser canvas only (frontend/level3/). Not the React account shell.

motion.value: width 1px to 84% lane, 90ms Cubic.Out; fade 360ms after 160ms

motion.name: reference-sink

motion.purpose: Verdict stamp landing on the transcript.

narrative.overview:
Scope. Everything here describes the Year 3 game surface only: the 1280 x 720 Phaser 4 canvas in frontend/level3/, mounted inside the shell's game workspace and allowed to go fullscreen. The surrounding React shell (dark navy, blue accents, sans UI) is a separate, incumbent system and is not governed by this file. Tokens live as TypeScript constants, not CSS: COLORS/CSS/SERIF/MONO/HAND in textures.ts, geometry in layout.ts, lane inks in config.ts. Sizes are logical canvas pixels at 1280 x 720.

The screen is a page of your own thesis open in a PDF viewer. Graphite viewer chrome frames one white sheet; on the sheet everything is either typeset (black Source Serif 4) or written by hand (red and blue ballpoint, Caveat). The rhythm lanes are Figure 3.1, a flat, booktabs-ruled four-column table; notes are references (Thm. 4.2, eq. (3.7), [42]) that you highlight on the beat with chisel-tip marker. The committee grades in red pen, and red marks persist, so the page ends up recording how the defense went. The verdict is a transcript of records with an inked rubber stamp.

The world refuses the rhythm-game default: no neon perspective highway on black, no glowing rails, no gamer HUD. Every element has to be something that could plausibly be on a printed thesis page or in the viewer around it. Density is that of a real LaTeX page: generous white, small precise rules, and two bold numerals that carry the score from three metres.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite PDF-viewer chrome around one white A4 sheet, drawn past the frame so fullscreen shows more viewer, never bands.
Two scripts only on paper: typeset Source Serif 4 and handwritten Caveat; Source Code Pro only for the file name and the `\begin{defense}` call.
Four highlighter inks as lanes; yellow is reserved for golden notes and Eureka.
Red ballpoint judges (misses, corrections, scars, stamp); blue ballpoint draws the professors and writes your hit words.
Flat booktabs geometry: constant-speed notes, no perspective, no glow.
Hand marks are wobbly and seeded: stable per element, never vector-straight.

rules.name: The Yellow Law Rule
rules.body: Yellow highlighter means golden: golden notes, Eureka, Space. A lane, label or celebration never uses it.

rules.name: The Two Pens Rule
rules.body: Red pen corrects and judges; blue pen doodles and praises. Ink colour tells the player whether the page is grading them or cheering them.

rules.name: The Grey Chrome Rule
rules.body: The viewer chrome is greys plus the selection blue. Highlighter inks appear in the chrome only in miniature, inside the page thumbnails.

rules.name: The Typeset-or-Handwritten Rule
rules.body: Every glyph on the sheet is Source Serif 4 or Caveat. No sans-serif on paper, ever; mono only where a file name or LaTeX source would appear.

rules.name: The Caption Rule
rules.body: Figures and tables are numbered and captioned like a thesis ("Figure 3.1:", "Table 1:", "Table 3.1:"). New panels on the page arrive as captioned tables or figures, not cards.

rules.name: The Flat Table Rule
rules.body: The lanes are a typeset table, not a road: no perspective, no vanishing point, constant note speed.

rules.name: The Ink-Not-Light Rule
rules.body: Emphasis is more ink, never light: no glow, no bloom, no blur. The hit rule swells in stroke width on the beat (2px to 4.5px over 160ms), it does not shine.

rules.name: The Pen-Never-Straight Rule
rules.body: Anything the committee or the candidate writes is drawn with `penLine`/`penCircle` or Caveat; only typeset rules are straight.

dos: **Do** keep this system inside `frontend/level3/`; the shell's navy and blue UI is a different world.
**Do** import colours, fonts and geometry from `textures.ts`, `config.ts` and `layout.ts` instead of restating hex values.
**Do** reserve highlighter-yellow for golden notes, Eureka and Space.
**Do** use red pen for judgment and blue pen for doodles and praise.
**Do** set new on-page information as a numbered, captioned table or figure with booktabs rules.
**Do** draw every hand mark with `penLine`, `penCircle` or Caveat, seeded so it stays stable.
**Do** draw backgrounds past the frame by `BLEED` so fullscreen shows more viewer.
**Do** keep the score, combo and grade as large bold serif numerals readable from three metres.
donts: **Don't** add perspective, a vanishing-point highway, glow, bloom or neon to the lanes.
**Don't** set sans-serif type on the sheet.
**Don't** use a lane ink or yellow in the viewer chrome outside the thumbnails.
**Don't** add shadows on the paper; the sheet shadow is the only one.
**Don't** put a tracked uppercase label above a heading as an eyebrow; tracked caps are for the running head, pane field names and meter labels only.
**Don't** use ETH logos or official marks; the transcript stays labelled unofficial.
